steps.text: Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a skillet over medium heat. Season salmon steaks with salt and pepper. Briefly fry salmon in hot oil until lightly cooked, about 2 minutes per side. Remove salmon to a plate and set aside.

Heat remaining 1 tablespoon oil in the skillet over medium heat. Cook onion and garlic in hot oil until fragrant, about 5 minutes. Stir in diced tomatoes and season with salt and pepper. Continue cooking until liquid from tomatoes makes a sauce, about 5 minutes more.
Return salmon to the skillet and simmer in tomato sauce until fish flakes easily with a fork, about 10 minutes. Stir beaten egg into sauce until incorporated; serve hot.

review.reviewBody: I made this tonight for dinner and we enjoyed it. I have used alot of recipes from this site and only make changes when I do not have what is called for as the case tonight. Along with the tomatoes I used 1 can of diced tomatoes(zesty chili) as I did not have enough fresh to double the recipe. Also I am not sure if the egg at the end is really needed, my family feels it would be fine without and just have more of a tomato style sauce. I served with pasta and salad. We will put this into one of our many favorites for the Lenten season. Thank you for a wonderful dish that could also be made with chicken for those folks that do not care for fish.

I have never been successful cooking salmon until now. Because I can't handle garlic or pepper, I substituted 1/4 cup of minced leeks for the garlic, and ground Grains of Paradise for the pepper. After researching other recipes online, I added 1/2 cup of water and a splash of fish sauce to the sauce and bringing to boil, and added 2 beaten eggs (instead of one). I turned off the heat and stirred until set, then added back the fish and simmered for 10 minutes, covered. So good.

I think this is now my fav pasta. I’m picky with my salmon too. With limits on shopping due to virus I used 1 1/2 cans of rotel. I first sautéed onion and garlic in butter then added salmon that I sprinkled Tony’s Cajun seasoning with. Once almost cooked firm I added a ago that I whipped with just a little half and half (only cream dairy I had ). Mixed it into pan and it turned into a cream chunky tomato sauce. Served over wheat spaghetti noodles. Oh. I add sugar to anything that is tomato based to rid the tart.

Lots of flavor. Served over brown rice, but not even sure it needed to be served over rice. I'm doing a yeast-free cleanse and this recipe was perfect. Will be making this again, and soon. I had fresh spinach on hand, and tossed some in at the end just before I added the egg. Only recommendation I would make is double the sauce because it is so good, you'll want more.
Loved it. Full of flavor. We left the salmon whole, so stirred in the eggs before putting the salmon back in. So delicious and more hearty than most salmon dishes.

This was very good (and second time I have made it)! The only adjustment I made was to use a can of drained diced tomatoes as I didn’t have fresh. I also broke up the salmon to make the sauté easier and for better mixing with the egg. I made once before and served over rice; this time I served with broccoli and crescent rolls on the side. It also did take about 40 minutes - I often find the time to make the recipes on this site take longer than stated, but this one was accurate. Very simple and very good. Has been added to our regular rotation at the request of my husband!
Ma Sarap, Lola... The only thing I added was 1 tablespoon of fish sauce when cooking the tomato. Served it with Shiratake noodles. Will definitely be making this again.

Tasty sauce and so quick and easy! I had to use a can of diced tomatoes because good tomatoes are out of season right now. My sauce turned out slightly pink because of the egg....make sure you beat the egg real well and stir quickly as you add to the sauce. I didn't taste the egg but it thickened the sauce up quickly. It worked great with my Salmon burgers, served over whole wheat pasta.

Loved this absolutely simple and hassle free recipe! (I also used canned diced tomatoes). I was hesitant about the egg at the end but I loved it. I found it killed a little of that tangy tomato taste that stays if you don't cook tomato sauce long enough. My husband also loved it and I will definitely be making this one often. Thanks for posting!!

I used tilapia instead of salmon with a light coating of S&P and flower before frying. I added a little bit of fish sauce too. Will make again because it was so simple and delicious. Thank you for sharing!
Was this a great meal ! Made it as posted and it turned out super! Like others I was worried about the egg but don’t leave it out. Will definitely be making this again
So very good and easy to make! Thank you for such a delicious dish! I served it over jasmine rice!
BF absolutely loved this one. I didn't use the egg and served over angel hair pasta. Yummy yummy yummy.
Great Recipee!! Did not have diced tomatoes so I added creamy tomatoe sauce and everyone loved it!!! EGGS NOT REQUIRED.....DO NOT RECOMMEND..
I'm giving it a 5 star because I went by the recipe and it was good. Thank you
I ended up using filets of steelhead for this and it came out really good. Especially over a bed of steamed rice
Absolutely delicious and very easy to cook!
